prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively name a single “best” lawyer — that depends on your case facts, budget, and what you want (highest settlement vs. trial readiness, for example). I can, however, tell you how to find a top personal-injury car-accident lawyer in Houston and offer to pull a short, ranked list for your ZIP code.

How to choose a great car-wreck lawyer
- Experience with motor-vehicle wrecks: Look for many car-accident cases (not just general civil practice).  
- Trial and verdict track record: Some cases must be tried to get fair value. Ask about jury verdicts and settlements for similar injuries.  
- Board certification: Texas has board certifications in relevant specialties (e.g., personal injury or civil trial law). That’s a strong quality signal.  
- Contingency-fee practice: Most PI lawyers work on contingency (you pay only if they recover). Confirm the percentage and who pays court/expert costs.  
- Communication and availability: Ask how often they will update you and who you’ll speak with day-to-day.  
- Client reviews and peer ratings: Check Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, AVVO, Google and Yelp.  
- Local litigation experience: A lawyer familiar with Harris County judges, local hospitals, and defense firms helps.

Good places to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral & Information Service  
- Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, AVVO  
- Google/Yelp reviews and Better Business Bureau  
- Local courthouse records (to check verdicts/filings)

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled car-accident cases like mine? What were the outcomes?  
- Will you personally handle my case or a team member?  
- What do you think my case is worth and why?  
- How long will it take?  
- What’s your fee structure and who pays costs?  
- Do you have trial experience and recent verdicts?

What to bring to the consult
- Police report, photos, medical records/bills, wage-loss documentation, insurance info, correspondence from insurers, names of witnesses.

Typical fees and timeline
- Contingency fees commonly 33%–40% if the case settles before suit; can vary for suit/appeal or if multiple lawyers are involved. Cases can take months to years depending on injuries and insurance disputes.

If you’d like, tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer a big-name firm or a smaller trial shop, and I’ll prepare a short list (3–5) of highly rated Houston personal-injury attorneys who focus on car wrecks, with contact info and why they might fit your needs.
